http_response.description:
A 57-year-old female without any medical history was admitted for evaluation of a left ventricular tumor that was discovered incidentally. The patient was asymptomatic and had no relevant past medical history. Physical examination findings were not specifically described in the case report.



Patient with medical imaging findings that require diagnostic interpretation

data.description: A rare benign vascular tumor of the heart composed of proliferating blood vessels; can arise in any chamber, including intramyocardial lesions of the left ventricle. Often an incidental finding on echocardiography or cardiac MRI.
symptoms_in_common: Imaging shows a well-circumscribed intramyocardial lesion visible on echocardiography and MRI
Adult patient (can occur at any age)
symptoms_not_in_common: No heart failure, arrhythmias, or embolic events (when symptomatic hemangiomas may cause these)

data.description: A benign fibrous tumor usually arising within the ventricular myocardium; most common in children but can occur in adults. Typically well-circumscribed and intramural in the left ventricle or septum.
symptoms_not_in_common: Adult age (fibromas are more common in children)
Absence of arrhythmias or conduction disturbances (often seen with fibromas)

data.description: An organized blood clot adherent to the endocardium, most often forming in regions of akinesis or dyskinesis after myocardial infarction or in severe cardiomyopathy.
symptoms_in_common: Mass within the left ventricle detected on imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: No history of myocardial infarction or cardiomyopathy
No reported left ventricular dysfunction or apical akinesis
Intramyocardial appearance rather than mural/apical endocardial attachment

data.description: The most common primary cardiac tumor, typically arising in the left atrium but rarely occurring in the ventricles. Gelatinous, often pedunculated masses that can be incidental or cause obstruction/embolization.
symptoms_in_common: Incidental intracardiac tumor detected on imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: Usual location is left atrium rather than left ventricle
Typically endocardial and mobile rather than intramyocardial
No constitutional symptoms (fever, weight loss) or embolic events

data.description: A small, benign, frond-like tumor typically arising from cardiac valves; can be incidental and is associated with embolic risk when mobile.
symptoms_not_in_common: Typical site is valvular rather than intramyocardial left ventricle
Usually a tiny, highly mobile, pedunculated lesion rather than a solid intramural mass

data.diagnosis: Primary cardiac sarcoma (e.g., angiosarcoma) or metastatic cardiac tumor
data.description: Malignant tumors involving the heart; primary sarcomas are rare and aggressive, while metastases to the heart are more common from extracardiac primaries.
symptoms_not_in_common: Patient asymptomatic without heart failure, chest pain, or pericardial effusion
Imaging suggests a well-circumscribed lesion rather than infiltrative or destructive mass
